name: Kandy Esala Perahera
venue_name: Sri Dalada Maligawa (Temple of the Tooth)
description: Ten nights of torch-lit processions - drummers, dancers, whip-crackers and robed elephants - carrying the sacred tooth relic through Kandy, climaxing on Esala Poya. Sri Lanka's biggest festival; book accommodation early.
source_note: srilanka.travel/festivals_year_around: held over 10 days, climaxing on Esala Poya

name: Vesak lanterns and pandals
venue_name: Colombo city (Gangaramaya, Beira Lake and roadside pandals)
description: Vesak marks the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and passing. Colombo fills with paper lanterns, illuminated pandals depicting the Buddha's life, and free food stalls (dansal).
source_note: srilanka.travel/festivals_year_around; dates = gazette Vesak Poya and the following public holiday

name: Poson pilgrimage at Mihintale
description: Poson commemorates the arrival of Buddhism in Sri Lanka at Mihintale, which draws huge crowds of pilgrims in white on Poson Poya.
source_note: Poson Full Moon Poya (gazette); Mihintale is the traditional centre of Poson observance

name: Duruthu Perahera
description: Annual procession at the Kelaniya temple, culminating on Duruthu Poya, commemorating the Buddha's first visit to Sri Lanka.
source_note: Duruthu Full Moon Poya (gazette); held at Kelaniya Raja Maha Viharaya

name: Sri Pada (Adam's Peak) pilgrimage season
description: The pilgrimage season, when the summit path is lit and the temple at the top is open; most climbers start around 2am to see sunrise from the peak.
source_note: Season runs Unduvap Poya (December) to Vesak Poya (May) - traditional dates
